figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Antimicrobial peptide sequence prediction from dental calculus using AMPcombi. (a) Geographical map showing the distribution of the
dental calculus metagenomes (DCMs) used in this study indicating the species, time period, and origin they represent. (b) A graphical summary
illustrating the workflow used to generate the input for AMPcombi, the intermediary steps and the downstream processing invoked to recover
putative AMP classes from the DCM. (c) Bubble chart demonstrating the proportion of successfully predicted AMPs derived from the different
DCM samples (small bubbles with sample codes) grouped by age period (large bubbles) using AMPcombi and data set specific filtering steps. The
color code of the different age periods is shown in (a). (d) The bar plots display the number of putative AMPs recovered per one million
nucleotides within the DCMs, while the stacked bar plot illustrates the proportion of the retained AMPs across the DCMs based on the prediction
efficacy of each AMP prediction tool included in the workflow. The color code of the different age periods is shown in (a). Six AMP prediction
tools were used in the workflow. HMMsearch was included as an additional sequence similarity−based method to capture known AMP motifs and
to standardize tool performance, but is not considered a prediction tool. Logo artwork by Anan Ibrahim, used with permission.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Recovery of ancient and oral-derived antimicrobial peptides from dental calculus. (a) The UpSet plot displays the number of AMPs
predicted by six AMP prediction tools and HMMsearch (a sequence similarity−based method) after removing peptides longer than 120 amino
acids and with AMP probability scores <0.8. The numbers above each vertical bar indicate the count of unique or mutually predicted AMPs by the
tools, while the horizontal bars indicate the total number of AMPs predicted solely by each tool in the data set. (b) Heatmap illustrating the final 78
clusters representing different putative AMP classes recovered from DCMs using AMPcombi and the subsequent filtering steps. The AMP clusters
are ordered by their total abundance among archeological human samples and are classified based on annotations obtained from UniRef100.19 The
heatmap color scale represents the number of AMPs recovered per cluster in each time period, with yellow indicating few AMPs and dark blue
indicating more than 70 AMPs, as shown in the scale bar.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Functional adaptation of paleo- and modern actifensins (PAF/MAF). (a) The pruned phylogenetic tree illustrates the clades in which
PAF/MAFI and PAF/MAFII are located (see Figure 3). In both clades, the paleo-representative is positioned basal to its modern counterpart,
suggesting potential structural and functional divergence over an evolutionary period. (b) The secondary structures predicted for each member of
the PAF/MAF I and PAF/MAF II groups. Superposition of the peptide structures was performed in PyMOL using the fit command. For PAF/
MAF I, the calculated root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) was 0.941 Å, while PAF/MAF II yielded an RMSD of 1.280 Å, indicating a high level of
structural similarity among the compared peptides. (c) The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values are expressed in μM and represent
the antimicrobial activity of each peptide against four different bacteria, revealing functional differences among the peptide variants. No
antimicrobial activity was observed for E. coli, i.e., its MIC could not determined (n.d.).
